sewing-machine.definition: A machine that joins fabric and other flexible materials by passing thread through them in linked stitches, usually with one thread above and another below.

thread.definition: A fine cord of twisted fibers (of cotton or silk or wool or nylon etc.) used in sewing and weaving.

bobbin.definition: A winder around which thread or tape or film or other flexible materials can be wound.

thimble.definition: As much as a thimble will hold.

pin-cushion.definition: A small padded object used to hold sewing pins and needles safely when they are not in use.
pin-cushion.exampleUsage: The tailor returned the pins to the pin cushion.

straight-pin.definition: A short, rigid wire with a pointed tip is used to fasten pieces of cloth or paper together.

seam-ripper.definition: A small sewing tool with a pointed hook used to cut and remove stitches.
seam-ripper.exampleUsage: The seam ripper helped remove an incorrect line of stitching.

sewing-scissors.definition: Sharp scissors designed for cutting fabric and sewing materials.
sewing-scissors.exampleUsage: The tailor used sewing scissors only for fabric.

rotary-cutter.definition: A cutting tool with a circular blade used to cut fabric or craft materials on a protected surface.
rotary-cutter.exampleUsage: The rotary cutter was stored with its blade covered.

tape-measure.definition: A flexible strip used for measuring length.

ruler.definition: A straight tool used for measuring and drawing lines.

fabric-marker.definition: A pen, pencil, chalk, or other tool used to mark temporary lines or points on fabric.
fabric-marker.exampleUsage: The fabric marker showed where the seam should be sewn.

chalk.definition: An amphetamine derivative (trade name Methedrine) used in the form of a crystalline hydrochloride.

cutting-mat.definition: A protective flat mat placed under material while it is being cut.
cutting-mat.exampleUsage: The fabric was laid flat on the cutting mat.

dress-form.definition: A body-shaped stand used by dressmakers to fit, drape, and display clothing.
dress-form.exampleUsage: The designer pinned the fabric on the dress form.

mannequin.definition: A woman who wears clothes to display fashions.

t-square.definition: A T-shaped measuring and drawing tool used to make straight lines and right angles.
t-square.exampleUsage: The pattern maker used a T-square to draw a straight line.

french-curve.definition: A curved template used in drafting and pattern making to draw smooth irregular curves.
french-curve.exampleUsage: The French curve helped shape the armhole line.

silk.definition: A fabric made from the fine threads produced by certain insect larvae.
silk.exampleUsage: The silk was identified during the lesson.

wool.definition: Soft hair from sheep, used to make warm cloth.

linen.definition: A fabric woven with fibers from the flax plant.

denim.definition: (used in the plural) close-fitting trousers of heavy denim for manual work or casual wear.

leather.definition: To whip with a leather strap.

chiffon.definition: A sheer fabric of silk or rayon.

velvet.definition: A silky densely piled fabric with a plain back.

corduroy.definition: A cut pile fabric with vertical ribs.

hook-and-eye.definition: A clothing fastener made from a small hook that catches on a matching loop.

snap.definition: The tendency of a body to return to its original shape after it has been stretched or compressed.

buckle.definition: To fasten with a buckle or buckles.

ribbon.definition: Any long object resembling a thin line.

lace.definition: A cord that is drawn through eyelets or around hooks in order to draw together two edges (as of a shoe or garment).

elastic-band.definition: A stretchable loop is used to fasten or bundle items together.

velcro.definition: Nylon fabric used as a fastening.

bias-tape.definition: A narrow strip of fabric cut diagonally across the grain and used to bind or finish fabric edges.
bias-tape.exampleUsage: The tailor used bias tape to finish the edge neatly.

collar.definition: A band of leather or rope that is placed around an animal's neck as a harness or to identify it.
collar.exampleUsage: The collar was identified during the lesson.

sleeve.definition: The part of a garment that is attached at the armhole and that provides a cloth covering for the arm.

cuff.definition: The lap consisting of a turned-back hem encircling the end of the sleeve or leg.

hem.definition: The edge of a piece of cloth.

lapel.definition: Lap at the front of a coat.

waistband.definition: A band of material around the waist that strengthens a skirt or trousers.

seam.definition: To put together with a seam.

dart.definition: To move along rapidly and lightly.

lining.definition: The act of attaching an inside lining (to a garment or curtain etc.).

fitting-room.definition: A private room where a customer can try on clothing.
fitting-room.exampleUsage: The customer checked the jacket in the fitting room.

full-length-mirror.definition: A tall mirror large enough to show most or all of a standing person's body.
full-length-mirror.exampleUsage: The full-length mirror showed how the garment fitted.

ironing-board.definition: A narrow, padded surface on folding legs supports garments while they are pressed with an iron.

steam-iron.definition: An electric household device heats water and presses fabric to remove wrinkles and form neat creases.

hanging-rack.definition: A horizontal rail or frame used to hang clothing on hangers.
hanging-rack.exampleUsage: Finished garments were placed on the hanging rack.

shelf.definition: A support that consists of a horizontal surface for holding objects.

drawer.definition: A sliding box in furniture used to store small things.

label.definition: A brief description given for purposes of identification.

order-form.definition: A written request for products or services records the selected items, required quantities, and purchaser’s details.

scissors.definition: A gymnastic exercise performed on the pommel horse when the gymnast moves their legs as the blades of scissors move.

pin.definition: To attach or fasten with pins.

iron.definition: To press and smooth with a heated iron.

fabric.definition: Artifact made by weaving or felting or knitting or crocheting natural or synthetic fibers.

elastic.definition: Capable of resuming original shape after stretching or compression.

interfacing.definition: A fabric or material added inside parts of a garment to give extra shape, strength, or support.
interfacing.exampleUsage: Interfacing helped the collar keep its shape.

dress.definition: To dress in a certain manner.

suit.definition: A set of garments (usually including a jacket and trousers or skirt) for outerwear all of the same fabric and color.

skirt.definition: A garment hanging from the waist.

trousers.definition: A garment (or part of a garment) designed for or relating to trousers.

vest.definition: A man's sleeveless garment worn underneath a coat.
